title: Incident — what a signal variant returns and what the app shows. DRAFT of the #37 output contract; the five required fields are frozen for the eval.

page_id.description: Article of the first insertion (fi page id).

inserting_rev_ids.description: Every revision that added or re-added the content. The eval matches on these.

removing_rev_ids.description: Every revision that took it out, oldest first.

tier.description: EvidenceTiers ids. No assessment yet → reverted.

score.description: Higher = stronger. Informational: rank is the array order.

total_exposure_seconds.description: Sum of the windows in which the content was live.

user_display.description: EditorDisplay.For(user).PlainText — IPs masked. Never the raw user string.

summary.description: EditorDisplay.MaskComment(comment): the edit summary as plain text with every IP address masked. Never the raw comment.

kind.description: Machine id of the signal. `examples` lists the known ids: first the ten tier reasons (TierReasonKind in snake_case, what TierRules produces and the app's pipeline emits), then four signals that do not move the tier. The set is open: a variant may add an id, and a consumer that does not know one shows `label`.

label.description: The signal in words, e.g. the TierRules reason text. Wording per docs/evidence-standard.md.

evidence.description: Short supporting text with every IP address masked: the removal reason for removal_reason, the first quote for claim_content.

tier_reason.description: Why the incident has its tier, as one sentence: TierRules.Assess(...).BecauseSentence = '<tier label> — because: <reason>, <reason>.' The same reasons are in `signals`.

assessment.description: The automated content assessment of the inserted text (P1.S9). null = not run, failed or over budget; the tier is then at most `reverted`.

confidence.description: How sure the assessment is of the category: 1 = a guess, 5 = certain.

quotes.description: The spans the model quoted from the inserted text, as it returned them. Not every quote is verbatim: a consumer that highlights them skips the ones it cannot find.

has_verified_quote.description: At least one of `quotes` occurs verbatim in the inserted text. TierRules needs this for level 2.

cluster_id.description: Claim cluster (P1.S7, #34): incidents with the same id repeat one claim. Always a string: write a numeric research.s7_cluster id as a string. null = not clustered.
